title: Unified Inference: Q3 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This document captures the Q3 2026 product overview, PRD, core design specs, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments). It is intended for product, engineering, GTM, and customer success teams as the canonical reference for scope, acceptance criteria, rollout plans, and customer-facing messaging.

1) Product overview

Goal: Provide a single, consistent inference API and operational experience across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments that optimizes for predictable latency, cost, and reliability. Unified Inference includes: model catalog and versioning, smart routing and fallback, batching & caching controls, quantization profiles, and per-route quality controls.

Key capabilities (Q3 2026 release):
- Unified REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Model variants and automatic fallback routing (latency/cost/compatibility policies).
- Per-route caching and batch configuration suggestions via Redwood Optimize integration.
- New rollout primitives: weighted canaries, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to eval suites.
- Enhanced observability: token-level cost breakdown, latency P50/P95/P99, and per-model quality deltas by prompt-set.

Target customers: engineering and ML teams at AI-native startups, mid-market product teams, and platform orgs managing centralized inference.

2) Problem statement and opportunity

Problem: Teams face high variance in cost and latency when moving from prototype to production due to ad-hoc serving configs, lack of reliable fallbacks, and limited visibility into per-token economics. Opportunity: By unifying runtime controls with productized routing, caching, and model management we reduce migration friction, lower unit costs, and preserve application reliability under load.

3) Success metrics (OKRs for Q3 2026 release window)

- Adopted_by_teams: 30 new Dedicated customers using "unified" routes within 90 days.
- Latency_improvement: 20% reduction in median token latency for 75% of high-throughput routes after recommended config adoption.
- Cost_delta: 15% average token-cost reduction for customers using recommended batching/quantization profiles.
- Reliability: <1% request error rate for served routes across Hosted and Dedicated with fallback policy enabled.

4) Product requirements (high level)

Must-have:
- Single API for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking with backwards-compatible parameter mapping.
- Model catalog: model id, version, flavor (fp16/int8/qat), and compatibility map.
- Routing policies: latency, cost, region, tier; with policy evaluation order and deterministic tie-break.
- Fallback chain: up to 3 fallback variants with automatic cost/latency-aware selection.
- Per-route SLO controls and automatic fallback on SLO breach.
- Integration with Redwood Optimize for per-route recommendations.

Nice-to-have:
- Per-customer default routing templates.
- Auto-generated migration suggestions for customers moving from single-model endpoints to multi-variant routing.

Non-goals:
- Full model training lifecycle (beyond onboarding and version pinning).
- Complex multi-tenant model sharing across Dedicated pools (not in scope for this release).

5) User stories and acceptance criteria

User story 1: As an ML engineer, I can define a route that uses model "rw-unify-1.0" as primary and falls back to "rw-unify-1.0-int8" when latency or capacity thresholds are exceeded.
Acceptance criteria:
1) Route config UI/CLI accepts a prioritized model list and policy.
2) System routes in-production traffic to fallback within 200ms of detecting target breach.
3) Metrics show fallback events and per-token cost before/after.

User story 2: As a platform engineer, I can view token-level cost by model and route for the last 30 days and export CSV for billing reconciliation.
Acceptance criteria:
1) Console exposes token-cost breakdown with P50/P95 latency buckets.
2) CSV export respects org-level access controls and includes model id, route id, tokens, cost.

6) Design overview and specs

Architecture summary:
- Control plane (catalog, route configs, rollout manager) remains multi-tenant hosted service.
- Data plane/serving runtime supports model variants with kernel selection and quantization-aware execution.
- Smart routing layer evaluates policies in this order: route-level overrides -> customer defaults -> global policies.

Key components and interfaces:
- /v1/routes API: create/update/delete route, attach model variants, set policies. (Backwards-compatible with existing endpoint API; new fields: variant_list, routing_policy, quality_guardrails).
- Model catalog schema: model_id, version, flavor, compatible_kernels, max_seq_len, memory_profile.
- Rollout manager: supports weighted canary with automatic rollback on quality regression or SLO breach.

Configuration table (example):
| property | type | example | description |
| route_id | string | customer-qa-embed | logical route name |
| variant_list | list[string] | rw-embed-1.1, rw-embed-1.1-int8 | ordered primary->fallback models |
| routing_policy | string | latency (p95<150ms) | policy to prioritize variants |
| batching | string | auto|cpu| suggested batching profile |
| quant_profile | string | qint8 | quantization profile name |

API compatibility notes:
- Default behavior keeps existing /v1/generate routes working; new optional JSON fields enable variant routing.
- SDKs will map legacy parameters to new routing objects automatically; deprecation window: 6 months.

Design trade-offs:
- Routing decision latency vs. accuracy of cost model: initial rollout uses a conservative estimator (safe fallback) with plan to phase in learned cost models in Q4.
- On-hosted control plane for Private deployments: control plane remains optional-hosted for Private customers with air-gap patterns documented in eng-private-deployments.

7) Observability and SLOs

SLOs (per-route default, configurable):
- Availability: 99.95% (monthly).
- Latency (p95 generation time): <= 350ms for short chat routes (<=128 tokens) on Dedicated tier.
- Error budget policy: automatic throttling and rolling fallback when error budget < 25% remaining.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Per-route dashboard: request rate, token-rate, cost-per-token, latency P50/P95/P99, fallback_count, quality_regressions.
- Alerting rules: p95 latency > configured threshold for 5m -> page owner_team; fallback_count spike -> Pager Duty to eng-sre.

8) Roadmap and themes (Q3 2026 -> Q1 2027)

Q3 2026 (this release): Unified routing, rollout primitives, console cost breakdown, Redwood Optimize integration for recommendations.
Q4 2026: Learned cost model, per-customer routing templates, UI for migration suggestions, expand fallback depth to 5 variants.
Q1 2027: Automated quality-aware routing (realtime evals with lightweight classifiers), on-device fallback support for edge deployments.

9) Pricing & packaging notes

Objective: Keep pricing transparent while differentiating between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private usage patterns. Pricing below is guidance for marketing and sales; final approved prices require finance sign-off.

Hosted API (usage-based):
- Text generation: base $0.015 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.06 per 1k completion tokens for rw-unify-1.0 flavor. Variant pricing adjusts by flavor (int8 = -30% completion token rate, fp16 = base).
- Embeddings: $0.0008 per embedding unit for rw-embed-1.x.
- Discount: committed volume tiers (10%, 20%, 35% at 1M, 5M, 20M tokens/month).

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Monthly reserved commit tiers: Small (4 GPUs), Medium (16 GPUs), Large (64 GPUs). Price = baseline infra + model compute premium. Dedicated customers buy a capacity seat and are billed for committed tokens above baseline at a discounted per-token rate (typically 40\u201360% of Hosted per-token price).
- Add-ons: Extended observability retention (+$2k/month), premium SLAs (+$5k/month), private registry (+$3k/month).

Private (VPC / on-prem):
- License fee (annual) + deployment & support package. Billing model customizable per contract; recommend price floor equal to 6 months Dedicated commit for comparable capacity.

Packaging guidance for sales:
- Offer an onboarding package (1-month ramp + two performance tuning sessions) at a fixed fee for Dedicated and Private deals.
- Migration credit: new Dedicated customers migrating from Hosted get up to $15k in credits toward the first 3 months if they commit to a 12-month contract.

Billing and metering notes:
- Token accounting must align across Hosted and Dedicated. Use the same tokenization library across products to avoid reconciliation drift.
- CSV export includes model_flavor and variant_id for accurate chargeback.

10) Release notes (v2026.3.0 - Q3 2026 unified-routing release)

Summary of changes:
- New: Route variant support with prioritized fallback chains (API: /v1/routes -> variant_list).
- New: Weighted canary rollouts with automatic rollback based on eval-set regression detection.
- New: Console: token-level cost breakdown and per-route export.
- New: Redwood Optimize integration: auto-suggest batching & quantization settings per route.
- Improved: SDKs (Python, Go, JS) now include route management helpers and automatic legacy parameter mapping.
- Fixed: Various edge cases in KV cache eviction that caused latency spikes at high concurrency.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Backwards compatible by default. Customers using legacy endpoint parameters will continue to work. To opt-in to variant routing, update route via /v1/routes or Console.
- Deprecation plan: legacy single-model route parameter names will be deprecated in 6 months; migration docs and CLI tooling provided.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Initial cost estimator is conservative and may route to higher-cost variants under uncertainty. Mitigation: enable Redwood Optimize and accept recommendations; learned estimator coming Q4.
- Some on-prem air-gapped deployments require a manual catalog sync for model metadata. See eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures for step-by-step.

Rollout plan and ownership:
- Staged rollout: internal dogfood (2 weeks) -> beta customers (4 weeks) -> general availability (GA) after successful beta.
- Owners:
  - Product: Ava Martinez (prod owner)
  - Engineering: Diego Alvarez (serving runtime owner), Priya Kapoor (control plane/console)
  - Eng-SRE: Liam Chen (rollout and incident runbooks)
  - GTM: Nora Patel (pricing & packaging lead)

Post-release follow-ups (30/60/90 days):
1) 30d: usage + adoption report; measure success metrics; capture top 5 migration blockers.
2) 60d: implement lightweight learned cost estimator pilot for top 5 customers.
3) 90d: evaluate expanding fallback depth and per-customer routing templates.

Appendix (commands and examples):
- Create route example (curl):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"route_id":"customer-chat-1","variant_list":["rw-chat-1.0","rw-chat-1.0-int8"],"routing_policy":"latency_p95<200ms","batching":"auto","quant_profile":"qint8"}'

- Export cost CSV: Console -> Route -> Export -> CSV (last 30 days).
